en: Points of Controversy Great Chapter Fifteen
Regarding the Discussion on Mutuality as a Condition:
Since volitional formations have ignorance as their condition, should it not be said that "ignorance also has volitional formations as its condition"?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that ignorance is co-nascent with volitional formations?
“Yes.”
If ignorance is co-nascent with volitional formations, then indeed it must be said:
“Volitional formations have ignorance as their condition, and ignorance has volitional formations as its condition.
Clinging has craving as its condition; it should not be said that [clinging has ignorance as its condition].
“Is craving also conditioned by clinging?”— Yes.
Is craving not co-nascent with clinging?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If craving is co-nascent with clinging, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
‘Clinging has craving as its condition, and craving has clinging as its condition.’”
“Bhikkhus, with aging-and-death as condition there is birth; with birth as condition there is existence”—is this indeed a sutta? It is not.
In that case, formations have ignorance as their condition alone; it should not be said that "ignorance also has formations as its condition.
Clinging has craving as its condition alone; it should not be said that...
“Craving also has clinging as its condition.
“Consciousness, bhikkhus, has name-and-form as its condition; name-and-form also has consciousness as its condition”—is there such a sutta?
“Yes, they do.
“In that case, formations have ignorance as their condition, and ignorance has formations as its condition;
clinging has craving as its condition, and craving has clinging as its condition.”
The Discussion on the Mutuality Condition is finished.
